lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 107, which opens every new split view at 50/50 and adds a --split option.
lines.say: This is a tour of pull request one oh seven, which opens every new split view at fifty-fifty and adds a dash dash split option.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
A split turns on: F3, the toolbar button, or a window that opens with split view already on.
By default it queues a 50/50 split; a hidden setting brings back the saved pixel position.
lines.say: By default it queues a fifty-fifty split; a hidden setting brings back the saved pixel position.

lines.caption: When the split pane gets its size, the divider is set to that size times the percentage.
When you drag the divider, it stays in that window and isn't saved, unless the setting is on.
New: thunar --split takes a whole number from 10 to 90; anything else is an error and opens nothing.
lines.say: New: Thunar dash dash split takes a whole number from ten to ninety; anything else is an error and opens nothing.

lines.caption: It always opens a new window, even with Open new windows as tabs on, one per folder.
That window turns split view on at the given percentage, applied the same way, and nothing is saved.
Before, one drag in a wide window made every later split open lopsided, because the position was saved in pixels.
The ratio waits for the pane's real size, because GTK rescales an earlier position from a possibly stale size.
Every way of turning split on goes through one function in the window code.
A new hidden setting, off by default, decides between the middle and the saved pixels.
The ratio is applied once, on the pane's next size change, by width, or by height in vertical split.
Your drag survives tab changes; the setting is checked at each drag, and closing split drops a waiting ratio.
A bad value prints Thunar's own error message, and the help text lists the new option.
The percentage travels with that one request, so other windows and later commands never see it.
The window keeps the percentage just until its split is applied, with the same folder in both panes.
By default F3 opens in the middle; with the hidden setting on, it opens at the saved pixels and saves drags.
Vertical split follows the same rules by height.
With the tab options, -T's split uses the percentage, and -t alone puts the first tab in the right pane.
lines.say: With the tab options, the right-pane option's split uses the percentage, and the left-pane option alone puts the first tab in the right pane.

lines.caption: A --split window skips restoring old tabs, and the value after -T isn't mistaken for a folder.
lines.say: A split window skips restoring old tabs, and the value after the right-pane option isn't mistaken for a folder.

lines.caption: This is the core change: the saved pixels only with the setting on, otherwise a queued ratio.
To get the old behaviour back, turn the hidden setting on; reverting the PR removes the setting and the option.
The PR changes six source files, including a small new size helper, and adds its test, this page and its narration.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows the test plans in issues 40 and 41, and keeps upstream's code behind the setting.
lines.say: It follows the test plans in issues forty and forty-one, and keeps upstream's code behind the setting.

lines.caption: The first twelve rows ran in this session before this round's review fixes; the test measures each pane from a screenshot.
It built and installed, and all 16 tests passed on the final code, the new one in 40 seconds.
lines.say: It built and installed, and all sixteen tests passed on the final code, the new one in forty seconds.

lines.caption: --split 60 gave 60 percent; the setting gave the saved 300 pixels; by default F3 opened in the middle.
lines.say: Split sixty gave sixty percent; the setting gave the saved three hundred pixels; by default F3 opened in the middle.

lines.caption: A drag stayed in its window, and with Thunar running, --split opened exactly one new window at 60 percent.
lines.say: A drag stayed in its window, and with Thunar running, split opened exactly one new window at sixty percent.

lines.caption: Bad values opened nothing, help lists the option, and the tab options gave 60 and 30 percent.
lines.say: Bad values opened nothing, help lists the option, and the tab options gave sixty and thirty percent.

lines.caption: Vertical split worked by height, and the saved position was still 300 at the end.
lines.say: Vertical split worked by height, and the saved position was still three hundred at the end.

lines.caption: CI's first run built the PR, passed the explainer, and its review found ten low findings.
This round's fixes compiled here; CI builds, verifies and reviews them after the push.
The test takes six screenshots, two of them before and after pairs.
A fresh review agent found five issues; three were fixed before the final test run.
The test now works on a dark theme, the ratio waits for the real size, and restored tabs no longer undo the split.
Two notes about the test were left, since neither can happen in the checks as written.
CI's own review found ten low findings and pushed no fix; its comment is linked here.
Fixed: turning the setting on or off now works even with a split already open.
Fixed: one shared size helper, and closing split view clears a ratio still waiting.
Fixed: a safer help check in the test, no application-wide new-window flag, and no new doc comment.
Four findings weren't changed, since the review didn't confirm them; they wait for your decision.
Your real desktop, including a maximized window, can only be checked after the merge.
The pull request, CI's comments and the two issues are linked here.
Part 3. Nothing depends on issues 40 or 41, so only a try on your own desktop remains.
lines.say: Part 3. Nothing depends on issues forty or forty-one, so only a try on your own desktop remains.

lines.caption: After the merge, press F3 in a wide and a small window, then try --split 60, also maximized.
lines.say: After the merge, press F3 in a wide and a small window, then try split sixty, also maximized.

lines.caption: In short: new splits open in the middle, and --split picks a ratio for one new window.
lines.say: In short: new splits open in the middle, and the split option picks a ratio for one new window.
